issues.legal_issue: A money decree against legal representatives for recovery from a deceased debtor’s estate can reach other property in their hands that is liable under Hindu law for the debtor’s debts, unless the parties expressly exclude that mode of enforcement.
material_facts: The decree was for money against the deceased debtor’s estate in the hands of his legal representatives.
The compromise did not expressly restrict enforcement to property inherited from the deceased debtor.
The decree-holder sought to execute the decree against property allotted to the debtor’s sons on partition.
issues.conclusion: Because the decree satisfied the requirements for a decree against legal representatives, the decree-holder could rely on the procedural provision extending execution to property in a descendant’s hands that was substantively liable for the deceased ancestor’s debt. The compromise did not exclude that right merely by remaining silent about it.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 52(1) and 53 of the Code of Civil Procedure, a decree for recovery from a deceased person’s estate may be executed against property in a son’s or other descendant’s hands that is liable under Hindu law for the ancestor’s debt. Section 53 is procedural and does not create substantive liability; a right to exclude the statutory mode of execution must be expressly stated and cannot be inferred from silence in a compromise.

rule.if: execution_against_legal_representatives and money_decree_limited_to_deceased_estate and descendant_property_substantively_liable and no_express_exclusion

predicates.execution_against_legal_representatives: A decree-holder sought execution of a decree against persons who were parties as the deceased debtor’s legal representatives.
predicates.money_decree_limited_to_deceased_estate: The decree ordered recovery of money from the deceased debtor’s estate in the hands of the legal representatives.
predicates.descendant_property_substantively_liable: Property held by a descendant was liable under the applicable substantive law for the deceased ancestor’s debt.
predicates.no_express_exclusion: The parties did not expressly agree to exclude enforcement against property otherwise reachable under the applicable procedure.

issues.definition: When execution is sought against legal representatives under a money decree limited to the deceased’s estate, and property in a descendant’s hands is substantively liable without an express exclusion, that property is reachable in execution.

issues.legal_issue: A son’s share received on partition remains liable for the father’s pre-partition debt if the debt is neither illegal nor immoral and no proper arrangement for its payment was made at partition.
material_facts: The father incurred the debt before the partition.
The sons received separate shares of family property on partition.
The debt’s legality or morality and whether provision for its payment was made at partition had not been determined.
issues.conclusion: A son remains liable after partition for the father’s pre-partition debt if it is not illegal or immoral and no arrangement for its payment was made when the partition took place.
issues.legal_principle: Under the Hindu-law pious obligation, a son’s liability for a father’s debt is limited to liable ancestral property and does not attach to the son’s self-acquisitions or create personal liability. The obligation continues after partition for pre-partition debts that are not illegal or immoral unless a proper arrangement for payment was made at partition. The Court relied on Hindu-law texts, Sat Narain v. Das, and Bankey Lal v. Durga Prasad, and approved the latter decision’s approach.

rule.if: claim_for_father_debt_against_separated_son and debt_incurred_before_partition and not debt_illegal_or_immoral and no_payment_arrangement_at_partition

predicates.claim_for_father_debt_against_separated_: A creditor sought payment of a father’s debt from a son who had separated from the father by partition.
predicates.debt_incurred_before_partition: The father incurred the debt before the family partition.
predicates.not debt_illegal_or_immoral: The debt was not illegal or tainted with immorality.
predicates.no_payment_arrangement_at_partition: No proper arrangement for payment of the debt was made when the partition took place.

issues.definition: When a creditor claims a father’s pre-partition debt from a separated son, the son’s partitioned share remains liable if the debt is not illegal or immoral and no payment arrangement was made at partition.

issues.legal_issue: A decree against sons as legal representatives of their deceased father for a pre-partition debt may be executed against property they received on partition without a separate suit, while allowing them to contest liability in execution.
material_facts: The debt was incurred before partition.
The father died while the creditor’s suit was pending, and the sons were brought into the suit as his legal representatives.
The decree was passed against the deceased father’s estate in the hands of his legal representatives.
The sons disputed whether their property was liable for the debt.
issues.conclusion: The decree could be enforced against property received by the sons on partition in execution proceedings, and a separate suit was not necessary. The sons could raise their objections to liability in those proceedings.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 47, 52(1), and 53 of the Code of Civil Procedure require questions concerning execution between parties or their representatives to be determined in execution proceedings. Section 53 treats property in a descendant’s hands that is liable under Hindu law for a deceased ancestor’s debt as property of the deceased for the relevant execution provisions. The Court approved the dissenting view in Atul Krishna v. Lala Nandanji and disapproved the majority view; it also approved Bankey Lal v. Durga Prasad. The procedure does not create or enlarge the underlying Hindu-law liability.

predicates.execution_of_decree_against_legal_repres: A creditor sought to execute a decree against persons made parties as the deceased debtor’s legal representatives.
predicates.sons_joined_as_representatives_after_fat: The sons were brought into the creditor’s suit as legal representatives after their father died.
predicates.debt_incurred_before_partition: The father incurred the debt before the family partition.
predicates.partition_property_substantively_liable: The property received by the sons on partition was liable under the applicable substantive law for the father’s debt.

issues.definition: When sons joined as legal representatives after their father’s death face execution of a decree for a pre-partition debt, property they received on partition that is substantively liable may be reached in execution without a separate suit.

issues.legal_issue: When a son is liable for a father’s debt, the executing court may direct the creditor to proceed first against property allotted to the father on partition and inherited by the sons, and then against the sons’ ancestral property for any remaining amount.
material_facts: The father received separate property on partition, and that property passed to the sons after his death.
The sons’ property received on partition was also potentially liable for the pre-partition debt.
The executing court was directed to determine whether the sons were liable and whether the father’s property was sufficient to satisfy the decree.
issues.conclusion: If the sons were held liable, the executing court could direct the creditor to proceed first against the father’s separate property allotted to him on partition and inherited by the sons, and to proceed against the sons’ ancestral property only for any shortfall.
issues.legal_principle: The Court stated that, if the sons were liable, the executing court could order resort first to the father’s separate property allotted to him on partition and later inherited by the sons, with execution against the sons’ ancestral property for any unsatisfied balance.

predicates.execution_for_father_debt: A creditor sought execution for a debt owed by a deceased father.
predicates.sons_found_liable: The executing court determined that the sons were liable for the father’s debt.
predicates.father_partition_property_inherited_by_s: Property allotted to the father on partition passed to the sons after his death.
predicates.father_property_insufficient_to_satisfy_: The property inherited from the father was insufficient to satisfy the decree.

issues.definition: When sons are liable, inherited property allotted to their father on partition is available first, and the court may permit recourse to their ancestral property for any remaining balance if that inherited property is insufficient.
